ai-ux-deslop: Use when an AI agent is designing, building, or reviewing any web or desktop UI (landing pages, tools, dashboards) and the result must not look like generic AI slop.
ai-workflow-doctor: Use to audit repo AI instructions, skill catalogs, references, provenance, duplication, context size or workflow drift; before/after instruction optimization.
brand-system-designer: Use this skill when the user wants logo design, brand identity, visual direction, color palette selection, typography pairing, SVG logo concepts, favicon creation, Open Graph assets, or a lightweight brand guide for a product, app, website, startup, or repo. Do not use this skill for general UI implementation unless the task is specifically about brand identity or visual language.
commit-dirty: Use when I explicitly want the current intended dirty git worktree committed and pushed now, including requests like `commit dirty`, `commit all dirty`, `commit and push this`, or `ship these changes`, after verifying scope and running the minimum relevant checks. Do not use for commit planning only, history rewrites, force-pushes, or work outside Git.
commit-plan-push: Use when planning dirty Git commits (`commit-plan`) or explicitly asked to plan, commit, and push or split and ship changes. Planning-only stays read-only.
commit-session: Use for `commit-session`, `ship this session`, or committing only this Codex session: commit and push session-owned Git changes, preserving pre-existing or other-session dirty work. Excludes planning-only all-dirty shipping and history rewrites.
context-handoff: Use for long tasks, acceptance criteria, progress.md, or handing off and resuming work after interruption, context compression, agent transfer, or a context-window boundary.
feedback-memory: Use for durable user corrections or preferences about workflow, formatting, style, tooling, review or communication, and sessions needing prior feedback.log guidance.
fish-alias: Use when adding or replacing a fish command, directory or file shortcut from an abbreviation plus a command or path in linux-config.
frontend-design: Use when building or redesigning frontend web interfaces such as pages, components, dashboards, or app UI.
grok-cli-handoff: Use for Grok Bot or remote assistant delegation to local Codex or Claude Code, cross-host CLI transfers, or delegated STOP.
hallmark: Design skill for websites and new pages that look designed, not generated. Use when the user asks to build or design something new, or names Hallmark. Never use it on an existing design unless the user names Hallmark, as in `/hallmark redesign <path>`.
impeccable: Explicit Impeccable design commands: critique, audit, refine, and build frontend interfaces.
last30days: Research what people actually say about any topic in the last 30 days. Pulls posts and engagement from Reddit, X, YouTube, TikTok, Hacker News, Polymarket, GitHub, and the web. Includes a doctor health check to diagnose broken or missing sources.
lean-instructions: Use when adding to AGENTS.md or adding, editing, or removing a skill.
metaprompt: Use for /metaprompt, "make me a prompt", or requests to create, sharpen, deepen, audit, or template prompts for models and agents.
metaprompt-run: Use when the user invokes $metaprompt-run, /metaprompt-run, or Metaprompt & Run, or explicitly requests prompt optimization followed by execution of the resulting task immediately in a new conversation with fresh context.
morning: Use only when I explicitly invoke `morning` to pick up after a `night` run. Read `NIGHT_NOTE.md` and the night branch's git history, summarize what happened, list up to five numbered A/B/C questions with recommendations, then act only on the answers I give.
next-tasks: Use only for explicit `next-tasks` or leftover weekly quota: propose evidence-backed tasks, wait for a choice, then execute it.
night: Use only for explicit `night` before stepping away: build one self-verifiable task unattended, commit and push checkpoints, and leave NIGHT_NOTE.md.
personal-context: Use automatically for personal or cross-project development/design choices: direction, scope, architecture, tooling, milestones or collaboration; explicit $personal-context discussions of motivations, tastes, goals and working experiences. Skip mechanical work.
playwright: Use when the task requires automating a real browser from the terminal (navigation, form filling, snapshots, screenshots, data extraction, UI-flow debugging) via `playwright-cli` or the bundled wrapper script.
postmortem-memory: Use for reported bugs, unexpected command/test/deployment failures, troubleshooting retries, or postmortem creation/updates.
readme-recruiter-sync: Use for README work, the pre-commit/push README gate, or changes to a documented public interface.
second-brain-session: Use when starting, continuing, capturing, or closing a example-user work session that needs established project/session context, ExampleProject progress, persistent instructions, or Second Brain retrieval. Personal-context retrieval and learning are a separate private workflow.
shadcn: Manage shadcn/ui components, project context, registries, presets and updates with the pinned CLI.
skill-eval: Evaluate and improve a named skill with real tasks, human-calibrated binary grading, and blind comparisons.
smoke-test-capture: Use when work in this repo introduces a concrete manual verification step, changes the expected outcome of an existing manual check, or exposes an obvious gap in the shared smoke-test checklist.
vercel-react-best-practices: Review React and Next.js performance using pinned Vercel Engineering guidance.
